title: Evaluation of the FeverApp as a documentation and information tool for the FeverApp registry during acute febrile episodes in children: Impact on parental decision-making and fever management in children aged three months to six years.
summary: The aim of the study is to examine whether the FeverApp, as a structured documentation and information tool, influences parental behavior in managing fever. The app is not intended as a therapeutic application but supports parents by providing evidence-based information and structured documentation of symptoms, medication usage, and temperature measurements. The goal is to assess whether the use of the app leads to a significant change in parental behavior in fever management, including the use of antipyretic medications. The focus is on changes in parental behavior, not on a direct evaluation of the app itself.
conditions: Fever of other and unknown origin

interventions.name: Intervention group: Participants in this group could use the FeverApp during their children's febrile episodes. The app is used to document temperature progression, symptoms, medication intake, and overall well-being, as well as to access evidence-based information from the information library.

Control group: Participants receive standard care without recomendation to use the FeverApp. They document their children's febrile episodes using a questionnaire without additional support from the digital application.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Informed Consent: Participants (parents) are able to provide informed consent and understand the nature of the study as well as their involvement in it.
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of Consent: Children whose parents or legal guardians do not provide consent to participate in the study.
No Access to Internet or Smartphone: Lack of access to the internet or a smartphone.
